### Logistic Regression

Logistic regression models the probability that a patient has heart disease
using the clinical predictors. Unlike linear regression, logistic regression
is designed for a binary response variable (0 = no heart disease,
1 = heart disease). It estimates the relationship between the predictors
and the log-odds of heart disease.

We use all predictors in the initial model and evaluate its ability to
classify patients using the same training and testing sets as the SVM.

```{r log-setup}
# Load packages needed for model evaluation
library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r log-fit}
# Fit logistic regression using all predictors
log_model <- glm(
  HeartDisease ~ .,
  data = train,
  family = binomial
)

# View model coefficients and significance
summary(log_model)
```

```{r log-odds}
# Convert coefficients from log-odds to odds ratios
odds_ratios <- exp(coef(log_model))

# Display odds ratios
odds_ratios
```

The odds ratios help interpret how each predictor relates to the odds of
heart disease. An odds ratio greater than 1 indicates higher odds, while
an odds ratio below 1 indicates lower odds, holding other predictors
constant.

```{r log-final}
# Predict probabilities on the testing set
log_prob <- predict(log_model, newdata = test, type = "response")

# Classify using a 0.50 probability threshold
log_pred <- ifelse(log_prob >= 0.5, 1, 0)

# Convert predictions and actual values to factors
log_pred <- factor(log_pred, levels = c(0, 1))
log_actual <- factor(test$HeartDisease, levels = c(0, 1))

# Create confusion matrix
log_cm <- confusionMatrix(log_pred, log_actual, positive = "1")

# Calculate ROC curve
log_roc <- roc(
  log_actual,
  log_prob,
  levels = c("0", "1"),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)

# View confusion matrix
log_cm$table
```

```{r log-results}
# Summarize model performance
log_results <- data.frame(
  Model       = "Logistic Regression",
  Accuracy    = round(log_cm$overall["Accuracy"], 3),
  Sensitivity = round(log_cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 3),
  Specificity = round(log_cm$byClass["Specificity"], 3),
  AUC         = round(as.numeric(auc(log_roc)), 3)
)

# Include the same baseline as the SVM section
baseline <- data.frame(
  Model       = "Baseline (always 'disease')",
  Accuracy    = round(mean(test$HeartDisease == 1), 3),
  Sensitivity = 1,
  Specificity = 0,
  AUC         = 0.5
)

log_results <- rbind(baseline, log_results)
rownames(log_results) <- NULL

log_results
```

```{r log-roc, fig.height=4, fig.width=5}
# Plot logistic regression ROC curve
ggroc(log_roc, legacy.axes = TRUE, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey") +
  labs(
    title = "Logistic Regression ROC Curve (Test Set)",
    x = "1 - Specificity",
    y = "Sensitivity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r log-export}
# Save predictions for the "Comparing Results" section
log_test_probs <- data.frame(
  actual = test$HeartDisease,
  logistic = log_prob
)
```
